stem:
Soham writes the prime factorisations $180=2\times2\times3\times3\times5$ and $12=2\times2\times3$.

Which claim about divisibility is correct?

options.text: $180$ is divisible by $12$ because both factorisations include the prime $2$.
$180$ is not divisible by $12$ because $180$ has prime factors that $12$ does not have.
$180$ is divisible by $12$ because $2\times2\times3$ from $12$ is included in the factorisation of $180$.
Whether $180$ and $12$ are co-prime settles whether $180$ is divisible by $12$.

teacher.key_rationale: 180 is divisible by 12 iff every prime factor of 12 appears in 180 with at least the same multiplicity; 2×2×3 sits inside 2×2×3×3×5. Sharing only some primes, reversing the inclusion, or switching to a co-prime test all miss that check.
